claim: A byte printed `L63 - 0 - R63` is one multiplier a side, the same pair on types whose front halves have nothing in common, and what stops it twenty-five decibels short of silence is not the multiplier. Read one band at a time the two channels separate by 33.7 decibels more in some bands than in others at the ends of the sweep and alike in all of them through the middle, against the same pair of channels with the effect taken out of the path separating alike everywhere to 0.1 of a decibel. A pair of multipliers has no frequency in it and cannot do that. Allow one term added after the pan and nineteen settings of twenty bands come back as one multiplier each, over 342 readings to a median of 0.17 decibels -- agreeing with the broadband balance to a tenth through the middle of the sweep and departing from it by two decibels at the last byte, which is where the broadband reading was reading the added term. The table's two sides are one table read in opposite directions, 0.54 of a decibel apart at worst over 17 settings, and its centre entry sits 2.44 decibels under its end -- neither the 3.01 of a constant-power pair nor the 6.02 of a straight crossfade.
whyNotNamed: The table is recovered and still unnamed. Every closed form in the catalogue falls away faster than it does, and half of every sweep is the table's own flat top where nothing that goes through the centre can be wrong -- so what decides is the other half. At byte 112, the last one the table is sure of, the three are 2.84, 4.99, 8.86 decibels out, against a table whose own reading repeats to a few tenths. The nearest of them is also the one that contradicts a property rather than missing a number: it holds the near side at unity to the centre of the byte, where the table has fallen 2.44 decibels. A table read off the measurement is the measurement, so what is published is a readout. What round one could not say and this can is that the entry is one number rather than one per band, which is what makes a closed form the right kind of thing to look for; and that how far the last entry goes is bounded from one side only, so a candidate taking it to silence is not refuted by anything here.
adds: The records say what each setting of the byte did to the two channels on three types, under three voices, and band by band. What is read out of them here is that the three types are one law rather than three; that a pair of multipliers cannot produce a separation with a shape in it, so a term is added downstream of the pan; that once it is allowed, one multiplier per setting accounts for every band of every setting; and that the multiplier so recovered is refuted by no closed form in the catalogue and refutes all three of them.
refutedBy: A setting of this byte on any of these types whose two channels land somewhere the published table does not put them, by more than the spread three voices produce at that setting. Or a band of one setting at which the two channels separate by what the recovered multiplier says while another band of the same setting does not, which is the one thing the added term is not allowed to do -- it is a term, not a filter on the pan. Or the same byte on a fourth type returning a different pair: two of the three here agree to 0.11 dB at every setting and the third to 0.93, so a type disagreeing by a decibel would say the tail is not one structure after all.
whatItWouldChange: Forty-three rows over thirty types stop being unknown as a shape and become known as a table that is not any of the obvious ones, with the reason the obvious ones fail now separated from the reason the output stops. A renderer panning these types with a sine-cosine pair would be right at the top of the byte and wrong by 3 decibels by byte 112 and further past it, which is the difference between an image that stays put and one that leaves the loudspeaker; and a renderer reproducing the stop as part of the pan law would put a floor under every panned signal that this unit only puts under what the pan has already taken down.

eraPriors.claim: The pair of multipliers is stored rather than computed, so it is free to have any shape at all.
eraPriors.why: A pan is two numbers worked out once, when the byte is written, by a control processor that does not compute a sine on demand. A hundred and twenty-eight settings of one multiplier is a hundred and twenty-eight bytes and the far side is the near side read backwards if the law is symmetric, so the whole thing fits in half of that. Nothing about the period argues for spending arithmetic to avoid it -- and once the table is free, what is in it is a taste decision made once at a desk.
eraPriors.wouldBeWrongIf: The pair landed exactly on a closed form at every setting, which would say the shape was computed and not chosen. Measured, it does not: the nearest candidate is out by a third of the span the two channels together move over.

eraPriors.claim: A panpot that stops short of silence is a design decision and not a failure.
eraPriors.why: An image that stays coherent at the extremes is what a machine meant to be mixed with is laid out for, and a table that stops costs exactly what one that does not costs.
eraPriors.wouldBeWrongIf: The same unit reached full separation on every pan it has. It does not reach it here and it does reach it elsewhere -- the part panpot returns 58.7 dB on the same two inputs -- so the two are different structures, and this prior explains why one of them may be shallow rather than that it is.

alternatives.reading: The pair is shared because the three types share one output stage, rather than because three separate stages were given the same table.

separatedBy.why_not_separable: Nothing this archive can measure. Two implementations of one table and one implementation reached three ways return the same two numbers, and the output is the only thing here that can be asked. The alternative stays open with the reason rather than being queued behind a run that could not answer it.

alternatives.reading: The far channel at the ends is not the pan's own floor but a fixed leak between the unit's two output channels, with the pan itself reaching silence.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: The band reading. A leak between two channels is a filter on the louder one, so the separation it produces is fixed in each band and the same under any signal; measured, the same band of the same note under two types puts the quieter channel four to nine decibels apart while the louder one agrees to two tenths of a decibel. Half of the reading stands, though, and is now the claim: that the pan itself may reach silence is consistent with everything here.

alternatives.reading: Something reaches the output without passing the effect's output stage, and the separation is the sum of a panned signal and an unpanned one.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: The type's output level written to zero with the pan hard over. Both channels then sit one decibel above the take's own lead, so there is nothing for a sum to have a second term of.

alternatives.reading: The compression is the voice's rather than the byte's, because the sweep was read through a single patch that is itself two signals.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: Three voices at six settings, ten decibels and a spectrum apart. The four in the middle agree to 0.87 dB, where the sweep's departure from the nearest closed form is a third of the span the two channels together move over.

alternatives.reading: The term added after the pan is the rounding of the pan's own multiply, rather than a noise the stage makes on its own.

separatedBy.why_not_separable: Both put a term in the quieter channel that does not scale with the multiplier and whose size follows what the stage was handed, which is all the output can be asked. What would tell them apart is the term's own spectrum against the signal's, and at the depth it sits the reading cannot hold a band steady enough to take one: at the last two bytes the bands of the quieter channel already move several decibels between adjacent settings of a byte whose broadband balance moves by a tenth.

reproduces.domain: The byte at nineteen settings on 01 01 and nine on 01 30 and 01 03, read as the difference between the two channels and as the two of them together, each against the setting the printed range calls 0.

residual.unit: share of the span the byte commands in that run
residual.why: Read as what the byte is printed to move. The floor is per setting and it is the spread three voices produce there, which is a tenth of a decibel in the middle and three at the ends -- a single floor would read the ends as the sharpest part of the comparison when they are the softest.

also_read_as.unit: share of the span, over the two channels together
also_read_as.why: The reading the catalogue says decides the class, and it does: three candidates that give the same difference to within a decibel or two differ by six in what the total does at the centre. It ranks them in a different order from the difference does, which is the finding and not a tie.

gates.name: gross
gates.why: The median residual over the span the effect commands, taken as the worst of the records scored. A rejection bound and not a target: below it the residual is reported and never optimised, because no candidate is decided by it.

gates.name: qualitative
gates.why: Properties the unit's readings have that the model's readings must have too. No arithmetic over a residual rescues a model that cuts where the unit boosts.

gates.name: power
gates.why: The runner-up in the catalogue, scored on the same records, and whether it leans or contradicts a property where the winner does neither. The decoy is not chosen -- it is whichever candidate came second, so a strawman cannot be put up in its place. A class holding one candidate is a catalogue that is unfinished, which is a finding and not a pass.

figures.beaten_by: contradicting a property the winner satisfies

gates.name: breakdown
gates.why: A point worse than 0.5 of the span is a failure at that point rather than error at it. A residual that leans with the setting or with frequency is pointing at a structure the model does not have; one that does not is pointing at the room and the converters, and is not made smaller by anything this project can do.

compared_against.why_not_a_filter: A balance record holds one run per directory of takes and does not carry a type or an address at its top level, so there is no index query that yields this set. What stands in for one is that every run in the record is scored except the three the run filed as controls, and those are left out by the scorer's own rule rather than by name: a setting whose name is not a byte is not a setting of the byte.

reproduces.what_survived_twice: No candidate and no verdict. Both readings return `rejected` and they do not agree on which candidate came first: the difference between the channels puts `the-far-side-alone-is-attenuated` ahead and the two together put `a-sine-cosine-pair` ahead by a factor of six. What both agree on is the qualitative gate, and on the same point -- every closed form here takes its far side to silence at the extreme setting, and the unit puts it 20.6 and 25.1 dB down on a chain that has separated by 58.7.
